featured.label: Wearable interfaces
featured.title: Learning personalized haptic perception
featured.fullTitle: A wearable input/output interface learns personalized models of haptic perception.
featured.authors: Wen Li, E. M. Adams, Z. Xu, J. Yao, A. Esmer, X. Ni, Bozhi Tian, Pedro Lopes
featured.description: A wearable haptic interface registers physical stimulation inputs and subjective perceptual outputs in a shared spatial coordinate frame. This enables personalized tactile and thermal perception models for perceptual prediction and inverse haptic rendering, with applications in VR, interpersonal haptic communication, and robot teleoperation.
featured.imageAlt: Wearable haptic input/output device with an electrode array on the forearm.

featured.label: Haptic perception
featured.title: Electrotactile Improves Thermal Referral
featured.authors: Wen Li, Rong Ni, Bozhi Tian, Pedro Lopes
featured.description: Electrotactile stimulation extends thermal referral to skin locations without thermal actuators. Compared with vibration-based referral, this improves cold referral and reduces distracting tactile sensations, enabling more realistic non-contact thermal experiences in VR.
featured.imageAlt: Study illustration comparing vibrotactile and electrotactile thermal referral in VR.

featured.label: Wearable bioelectronics
featured.title: Hydrogel electrochemical cell for hydrogen therapy.
featured.fullTitle: Hydrogen evolution and dynamics in hydrogel electrochemical cells for ischemia–reperfusion therapy.
featured.authors: Wen Li, Jing Zhang, et al., Bozhi Tian
featured.description: A hydrogel electrochemical cell uses the hydrogel as the electrolyte, reaction medium, and therapeutic delivery reservoir. It integrates hydrogen generation, local storage, and sustained release for electronically controlled, localized delivery, validated in preclinical ischemia–reperfusion and pressure-ulcer models.
featured.imageAlt: Research figure illustrating a portable hydrogel electrochemical device for hydrogen delivery.

publications.title: Gold-modified nanoporous silicon for photoelectrochemical regulation of intracellular condensates
publications.authors: Jing Zhang, Pengju Li, Jiping Yue, Lingyuan Meng, Wen Li, et al., Bozhi Tian
publications.imageAlt: Scientific figure from the nanoporous silicon photoelectrochemical study.
publications.abstract: Gold-modified nanoporous silicon generates hydrogen peroxide under physiological conditions and regulates intracellular stress granules through extracellular photoelectrochemistry. This links light-controlled chemical production to cellular stress responses, with protective effects evaluated in an ex vivo myocardial ischemia–reperfusion model.

publications.title: Monolithic silicon for high spatiotemporal translational photostimulation
publications.authors: Pengju Li, Jing Zhang, Hidenori Hayashi, Jiping Yue, Wen Li, et al., Bozhi Tian
publications.imageAlt: Scientific figure from the monolithic silicon photostimulation study.
publications.abstract: Monolithic silicon interfaces enable leadless, multisite optical stimulation without genetic modification, addressing constraints of wired electrode arrays and supporting minimally invasive cardiac pacing.

publications.title: Perspectives on Multiscale Colloid-Based Materials for Biomedical Applications
publications.authors: Wen Li, Judah Huberman-Shlaes, Bozhi Tian
publications.imageAlt: Overview of multiscale colloid-based materials for biomedical applications.
publications.abstract: A perspective connecting nanoscale chemistry and microscale structure in colloidal materials to macroscopic biointerfaces. It links design across these scales to biomedical opportunities in spatial imaging, localized delivery, and interactions with biological systems.

publications.title: A strong and rigid coordination adaptable network that can be reprocessed and recycled at mild conditions
publications.authors: Wen Li, Hong-Qin Wang, et al., Cheng-Hui Li
publications.imageAlt: Scientific figure showing a coordination adaptable polymer network.
publications.abstract: Coordination adaptable polymer networks combine mechanical strength and rigidity with reprocessing and recycling under mild conditions. Reversible metal–ligand bonds address the tension between strong networks and material recovery, allowing reuse without sacrificing mechanical performance.
